{
  "repository": "https://github.com/t4t5/rencal",
  "files": [
    "LICENSE",
    "README.md",
    "src/components/main/month-view/MonthView.tsx",
    "src/components/main/month-view/Grid.tsx",
    "src/components/main/month-view/Row.tsx",
    "src/hooks/cal-events/useMonthGrid.ts",
    "src/hooks/cal-events/useMonthEventLayout.ts",
    "src/lib/api/calendar-events.ts"
  ],
  "rationale": "renCal is a real, shipped desktop calendar application (Tauri 2 + React + TypeScript, ~1,000 commits, 179 stars, MIT) — not a display-only component library — and it is the closest verified match to the supplied scenario while keeping the leaf's defining core intact: user-managed events anchored to a date/time, accumulated in a persistent schedule, presented on the application's own navigable month time grid.\n\nScenario fit, verified by reading the pinned source:\n- Real seven-column month grid: Row.tsx renders `grid grid-cols-7` for both the day-number strip and the event area; useMonthGrid.ts builds weeks as exactly 7 `Temporal.PlainDate` values (`for (let d = 0; d < 7; d++)`) from a month range. This is a genuine month grid, not a list.\n- Switchable previous/next month and navigable history: MonthView.tsx wires `useInfiniteMonths` + `useCalendarNavigation`; Grid.tsx anchors the scroll to the active month and re-centers on navigation (`virtualizer.scrollToIndex(weekIndex)`), while useInfiniteMonths.tsx (verified, adjacent) prepends earlier months when scrolling toward the top, so historical months stay reachable.\n- Create / read / edit / reschedule / delete of own events with title, start/end datetime, optional location and notes: calendar-events.ts exposes the full app-facing CRUD (`createEvent`, `listEvents`, `replaceEvent`, `deleteEvent`) over a `CalendarEvent` record carrying `summary`, `start`, `end`, `description`, `location`, `url`. The editor surface (src/components/event-parts/EditEvent.tsx, verified) binds those fields and triggers delete; reschedule-by-move is implemented in src/lib/event-drag.ts (verified), which shifts start and end together so duration is preserved.\n- Half-open [start, end) intervals and cross-day/cross-month visibility: calendar-events.ts documents and implements the viewer-zone half-open range contract for `listEvents`; useMonthEventLayout.ts routes each event into the correct day column of the intersecting week (`timedByCol` indexed 0-6) and routes multi-day events into the spanning all-day lane via `clipSpanToRange`, which clamps a span to the visible range — exactly the "visible in intersecting months" rule.\n- Overlaps allowed and displayed rather than rejected: useMonthEventLayout.ts places every timed event into its day column and sorts by start time; there is no conflict rejection path, and Cell.tsx renders up to four timed blocks per cell plus a '+n more' summary — overlaps are shown, not refused.\n- Persistence across restarts: README.md states events are stored as plaintext `.ics` files on the local machine (local-first, plaintext), so reopening the app restores the schedule.\n- Fixed UTC+08:00 without DST: the time model is Temporal-based and explicitly wall-clock-first. The event-time module distinguishes `datetime_floating` / `datetime_zoned` / `datetime_utc` and documents in docs/event-time-system.md that scheduled events should be treated as wall-clock time so a fixed-offset zone (Asia/Shanghai, no DST) keeps its clock reading. The adapter for this scenario pins `getViewerTzid()` to a fixed UTC+08:00 identifier rather than reading the OS zone.\n\nThe P0 exclusions are satisfied by trimming, not by the upstream project: upstream additionally ships recurrence (RRULE), invitations/RSVP, CalDAV account sync, notifications and viewer time-zone switching. Those surfaces are precisely what the scenario forbids at P0, so the adapter keeps the event model, the month grid, and the local `.ics` persistence, and drops the recurrence/sync/invitation/timezone-switch layers. The lead's caution against passing off a display-only library as an application does not apply here — renCal is a full application with its own event editor, drag-to-create, drag-to-reschedule and on-disk store.\n\nThe selected surface is deliberately small: eight focused files (license, README, month-view composition/grid/row, two month-layout hooks, and the CRUD boundary), each a small text source file well under the 180KB cap.",
  "alternatives": [
    "https://github.com/nextcloud/calendar — the supplied lead. Verified real and open source (AGPL-3.0, 1.2k stars) and it does render a month grid and an event editor, but it is a Nextcloud server app: it requires an account and a CalDAV backend, and it delegates its month view to the fullcalendar component library. The scenario is a local single-user P0 with no accounts and no sync, so upstream's mandatory server/identity layer is out of scope. Copyleft AGPL is also a weaker licensing fit than MIT.",
    "https://github.com/x3me/omacal — verified MIT, Tauri + Rust + Svelte, real application with local database storage and a CLI. Rejected because it is built around connecting Google/iCloud/CalDAV accounts with a keyring, i.e. exactly the account/sync surface the scenario excludes at P0, and its grid work concentrates on a week/time-grid rather than a seven-column month grid.",
    "https://github.com/FossifyOrg/Calendar — verified real calendar application (GPL-3.0, 2.2k stars) with a month view, event editor and local storage. Rejected mainly on licensing (copyleft GPL rather than permissive) and platform (Android/Kotlin), and it bundles sync to Google/Outlook/Nextcloud that P0 excludes.",
    "https://github.com/tianjiashu/desktop-calendar-tauri (DayPilot) — verified MIT, local-first SQLite, and notably interprets all times as Asia/Shanghai, i.e. a fixed UTC+08:00 with no DST, which matches the scenario's zone rule. Rejected because its UI is a floating widget plus a seven-day week view with a time grid; it has no seven-column month grid, so it cannot ground the defining 'month time grid' surface of the leaf.",
    "https://github.com/rtvkiz/cal — verified MIT terminal calendar with month/day/agenda views and JSON persistence (~/.cal/events.json). Rejected as a TUI reference for a GUI month time grid and as too small a surface to ground event editing semantics."
  ],
  "search_notes": "Searched for open-source GitHub calendar applications matching the scenario (local single-user, seven-column month grid, event create/read/edit/reschedule/delete, title + start/end + optional location/notes, fixed UTC+08:00, half-open intervals, cross-month visibility, overlapping events allowed and shown, reopen-persistence). Queries covered 'open source calendar app GitHub month view grid create edit delete events local single user MIT license', 'GitHub small local-first calendar app month grid event editor SQLite TypeScript self-hosted', 'open source calendar app Rust Svelte month view grid create edit event local database sqlite', and 'calendar desktop app MIT license month view create edit delete events sqlite local offline github tauri electron 2026'. Repository listing pages and raw file contents were fetched directly for each candidate; the GitHub REST API host was not reachable from this environment, so tree listings and raw.githubusercontent.com were used for path and content verification.\n\nLead verification: nextcloud/calendar was confirmed live and real (AGPL-3.0, 'Calendar app for Nextcloud', 10,896 commits, month view via fullcalendar, Attendees/Free-Busy/Reminders/Search/Tasks features, PHP + Vue frontend with composer.json, lib/, src/ containing fullcalendar/, models/, store/, views/). It was not selected for the reasons given above (server/account dependency, copyleft, delegated grid component) — the task allowed a smaller real calendar application with verified event-editing and time-grid code.\n\nFor the selected repository t4t5/rencal, every listed path was fetched at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/t4t5/rencal/main/<path> and returned its real contents (LICENSE = MIT 'Copyright (c) 2026 t4t5'; README.md; MonthView.tsx; Grid.tsx; Row.tsx; useMonthGrid.ts; useMonthEventLayout.ts; api/calendar-events.ts). Additionally verified but not selected, to keep the surface at eight files: src/components/main/month-view/useInfiniteMonths.tsx, src/components/main/month-view/Cell.tsx, src/components/main/month-view/useDragToCreateDays.ts, src/lib/event-drag.ts, src/lib/cal-events.ts, src/lib/event-time/{index,edit,local-zone}.ts, src/lib/event-time/types.ts, src/contexts/CalendarStateContext.tsx, src/components/event-parts/EditEvent.tsx, src/components/main/MainHeader.tsx, docs/event-time-system.md, docs/drag-to-reschedule.md, src-tauri/src/routes/caldir/*.rs.\n\nNo commit hashes, tags, release numbers or license versions are asserted beyond what the fetched LICENSE, README and repository pages state; the repository identity is the default-branch repository root, with no branch URLs."
}
